app.name: Xi Control
settings.title: XiControl Settings
settings.features.sub: Which features to show in the menu and panel.
settings.language.desc: Language of the menu, panel and pop-ups.
settings.autostart.desc: Via Task Scheduler, without a UAC prompt.
settings.brightness.desc: Separately for AC and battery; no Power profiles.
settings.battery.sub: Charge threshold, travel mode and the charge-ready sound.
settings.battery.note: The battery-care threshold is picked from the values your firmware supports (an arbitrary percent isn’t possible). The threshold/100% toggle itself lives in the tray and panel as a quick action.
settings.battery.care.limit.desc: Charge up to this level while “Battery care” is on. The threshold ↔ 100% toggle lives in the tray and panel.
settings.travel.sound.desc: A jingle when the battery reaches 100%.
settings.travel.lock.sound: Travel sound on the lock screen
settings.travel.lock.sound.desc: Jingle when the mode is toggled by a key while the screen is locked (the OSD is not visible there).
settings.travel.lock.toast.desc: Toast notification about Travel toggling while the screen is locked.
settings.travel.lock.note: To see the notification text, open Settings → System → Notifications → XiControl and disable “Hide content when notifications are on the lock screen”. You can also mute the notification sound there — otherwise the system chime plays together with the jingle.
settings.charger.watts.desc: Wattage of the connected adapter when charging starts (PD adapters only).
settings.charger.weak.desc: If a connected adapter is below this wattage — an OSD warns about slow charging.
settings.battery.health.desc: Current maximum capacity relative to the design capacity.
settings.battery.cycles.desc: Full charge cycles the battery has been through.
settings.display.sub: Refresh rate depending on the power source.
settings.hz.auto.desc: Higher on AC, lower on battery — saves power.
settings.hz.hold.desc: Restore the configured rate if Windows or another app changes it. Requires the option above.
settings.hz.ac.desc: If the exact rate is missing — the nearest is used.
settings.hz.note: The screen may briefly flicker or go black when the refresh rate changes — that’s normal, the display is switching modes. If the target rate is already set, nothing is switched.
settings.show.full.desc: Maximum mode. Off — removed from menu and panel.
settings.start.restore.desc: Remember the chosen mode and apply it at startup.
settings.start.pin.desc: Always apply the same mode at boot.
settings.start.profiles.desc: A separate performance mode on AC and battery.
settings.keys.sub: Actions of the Mi button and dead keys — assign any function to each.
settings.keys.mi.hold: Holding the Mi button always opens the quick panel.
settings.key.mi.click.desc: A short press of the Mi button.
settings.key.mi.double.desc: “Nothing” disables the gesture; single click fires instantly.
settings.key.settings.desc: The gear key. While the panel is open it always toggles charge.
settings.owl.feature.desc: Show the owl in the panel and menu (keep screen on / no sleep).
settings.touchpad.feature.desc: Panel cell and key action. A disabled touchpad always re-enables itself after a reboot.
settings.touchscreen.feature.desc: Panel cell and key action. A disabled touchscreen always re-enables itself after a reboot.
settings.refresh.feature.desc: Menu item, panel cell and the Display tab. Turn off if you don't need auto Hz switching.
settings.touchpad.deadzone.desc: Don't start a touch in the bottom strip — protection from a resting palm.
settings.touchpad.deadzone.size.desc: Measured from the bottom edge of the pad. Requires the option above.
settings.touchpad.deadzone.note: Only the start of a touch is suppressed: a finger first placed in the strip doesn't move the cursor and doesn't tap. A gesture started higher up keeps working all the way down, and pressing inside the zone still clicks.
settings.touchpad.deadzone.aap: The zone is inactive right now: touchpad sensitivity in Windows settings is set to maximum, which turns palm rejection off entirely. Pick a lower sensitivity.
settings.log.desc: The %APPDATA%\XiControl\log.txt journal — useful for bug reports. Off — nothing is written at all.
settings.api.sub: Web API for control over your local network (phone, Home Assistant). Off by default; settings live in %ProgramData%\XiControl\api.json and can only be changed by an administrator.
settings.api.enable.desc: Local web server with a whitelisted set of commands; state is read via GET /status. When off, the server does not run at all.
settings.api.lan.desc: Warning: the API becomes reachable by every device on your local network that knows the token. Off — this computer only (127.0.0.1). The firewall rule is created and removed automatically.
settings.api.token.desc: Only a SHA-256 fingerprint is stored. The token is shown once — copy it right away.
settings.api.cmd.owl.desc: POST /owl — toggle “keep awake”. Available while the owl is enabled on the Features tab.
settings.about.sub: Driver-free tray utility for Xiaomi / Redmi laptops.
settings.about.note: No kernel drivers, WinRing0 or direct EC access. Everything goes through the firmware’s WMI interface and Win32.
panel.title: Quick settings
monitor.title: Monitor
osd.hz.on.sub: {0} Hz on AC, {1} Hz on battery
settings.flyout.theme.desc: Quick panel, OSD and Monitor: dark, light, or follow Windows.
toast.firstrun.title: XiControl is running in the tray
toast.firstrun.text: Click the tray icon for the quick panel, right-click for the menu. Holding the Mi button also opens the panel.
err.title: Error
err.noiface: MIFS interface not found. Requires administrator rights and a compatible Xiaomi/Redmi laptop.
